Commentary.Commentary: Time for the action to begin now in this afternoon session. Imam-ul-Haq and Abdullah Shafique are the openers. Mitchell Starc to begin.
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Saying that, we feel the Aussies have a good score on the board. The wicket is not the easiest to bat on. The ball was doing a bit, it also has seemed to have quickened up and hence, we feel, the Aussies have a competitive total. None of their batters scored a big ton but there were handy contributions from a few of them. Marnus Labuschagne was the highlight with a hard-fought fifty-plus score. A few others got off to starts but none went onto make it into a big score. Now it is onto their bowlers and we believe they will be rearing to bowl on this wicket. Pakistan on the other hand, have a stiff task ahead of them but they have momentum on their side, can they show some fight with the bat now? We will find out. Join us in a bit.

That is fine, fine session for Pakistan! Just the kind they would have hoped for this morning. The start was not the best for them as Head and Marnus Labuschagne were dealing in boundaries but once Head fell, wickets fell at regular intervals. The likes of Mir Hamza, Aamer Jamal and Shaheen Afridi were really good. Yes, they will be a little disappointd with how quicly they have let Australia score in this session but they will be pleased to have bowled them out for the score they have done. All the bowlers got a wicket at least but have to say, Aamer Jamal and Mir Hamza were the pick this morning.

A really intriguing day of Test cricket is what we witnessed on the first day! Pakistan probably made the right call at the toss to elect to field but failed to capitalize. The ball did do its bit, there was good amount of movement and some nice zip off the surface but some poor fielding and some inconsistent bowling meant the Aussies found a way to survive the challenging phase. Yes, the going was slow but the platform is laid for them to post a challenging first innings score. Marnus Labuschagne is well set and Travis Head has looked solid so far in the 19 balls he has faced. Have to believe, the conditions for batting will be a lot better and the Australian batters would want to feast on that.

There was a brief rain break in between but Pakistan kept it tight after the break as well. Marnus Labuschagne survived a couple of LBW shouts but Smith didn't as he edged one to the keeper. Right now, Marnus Labuschagne looks in full control of his innings and he will hope to build a strong partnership with Head on Day 2 while Pakistan will hope to keep hitting those lengths, find some swing and get wickets as quickly as possible. A decent start to the Boxing Day Test match. Both teams will be happy at the moment. Pakistan asked Australia to bat first and once again, the veteran duo of Usman Khawaja and David Warner gave a wonderful start to their team. The ball swung both ways but Australia were disciplined while batting however, just at the stroke of Lunch, David Warner went for a big drive and edged it to slip. Pakistan started the post-lunch session on a bright note, keeping the pressure intact and got the other opener as well.

That wicket right towards the end will make Pakistan feel a little better but we have to say, it is Australia's session! It was not easy to bat early on, the ball was swinging both ways and there was some uneven bounce too. David Warner did provide a chance early on but that was not taken. The openers then went onto add 90. It seemed like it would be a wicket-less session but Agha Salman towards the end struck. Pakistan will hope, that opens the floodgates for them and they get a few quickly after the break. Australia on the other hand, will hope the batters to come can build on the foundation laid by the opening stand. Join us after the break for an important second session.

It is time for the second Test between Pakistan and Australia and the action shifts to Melbourne. The hosts put on a clinical performance in the first game and thrashed the visitors by a massive margin. We expect the Aussies to be dominant in this game as well but Pakistan is one side you can't take lightly. They are quite unpredictable and are well and truly capable of besting the best on their day. For that though, they'll have to be at their best if they are to have any chance against this Australian side. Can they put the loss behind and come back strongly in this game? We will find out. For now, let's hope we have an equal contest between bat and ball.
